candidate_relations.reason: Although the imaging shows classic AIP features (sausage-shaped pancreas, capsule-like rim, diffuse narrowing of MPD), the clinical picture strongly favors malignancy: markedly elevated CEA (28.8 ng/mL) and CA19-9 (76.6 U/mL), FDG-PET with high SUVmax in pancreas (8.6) and multiple hypermetabolic lymph nodes (10.0), new-onset diabetes (HbA1c 7.2%), and normal serum IgG4 ruling out type 1 AIP. AIP type 2 is a related differential but is an incompatible diagnostic entity given the tumor markers, PET findings, and lymphadenopathy pattern consistent with pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Autoimmune pancreatitis type 2 is a benign inflammatory condition; reference diagnosis is pancreatic adenocarcinoma, a malignant neoplasm

case_quality_flags: Imaging mimics AIP but tumor markers, PET hypermetabolism with nodal involvement, and normal IgG4 collectively support pancreatic adenocarcinoma over autoimmune pancreatitis
